corePrinciples.reputationProtection: B2B buyers are not spending their own money but ARE protecting their professional reputation. The fear of making a wrong, visible, expensive mistake is a primary motivator. Always reduce perceived risk.
corePrinciples.rationalVsEmotional: B2B buying decisions feel rational (ROI, specifications, warranties) but are primarily emotional (prestige, security, confidence in the supplier). Speak to both levels.
socialProofHierarchy: Before/after project photography with a named Australian client
Industry-specific testimonials (law firm praising TCD for a law firm audience)
ISO/certification badges — quality signals that require no explanation
Warranty length — 6-year signals serious quality commitment

CEO_MD.primaryMotivation: Vision realisation — the office as a statement of success and culture
CEO_MD.fearOf: Making the company look unsuccessful or behind competitors
CEO_MD.whatResonates: Show how the office positions the brand. Use aspirational language. Reference comparable companies.
CEO_MD.howToInfluence: Speak to vision and brand identity. Present the Executive tier first. Name-drop comparable company types.

CFO.primaryMotivation: Certainty of value and risk elimination
CFO.whatResonates: Total cost of ownership, warranty savings vs replacing cheap furniture at year 2–3, milestone payment structure
CFO.howToInfluence: Provide itemised quote. Explain 6-year warranty vs industry-standard 1-year. Offer 30/30/40 milestone payments on large projects.

OfficeManager_EA.primaryMotivation: Executing successfully and avoiding blame for poor decisions
OfficeManager_EA.fearOf: Choosing a supplier who fails to deliver on time, causing disruption
OfficeManager_EA.whatResonates: Project certainty, responsiveness, clear timeline milestones, easy communication
OfficeManager_EA.howToInfluence: This is your internal champion — equip them with everything to sell internally. Comparison summary, presentation deck, FAQ document, timeline.
OfficeManager_EA.importance: Most critical influence target — they research, recommend, and coordinate. If they champion TCD internally, the deal closes.

ITManager.fearOf: Furniture installed in wrong positions, AV incompatibility, power routing issues
ITManager.whatResonates: Confirm cable management specifications, coordinated delivery after IT cabling
ITManager.howToInfluence: Offer to coordinate directly with IT on AV and cable management spec before order placement

psychologicalTriggers.anchoring: The first price presented becomes the reference point. Always anchor high. A client who moves down from Executive to Professional is psychologically committed; one who moves up from Foundation is not.
psychologicalTriggers.lossAversion: Loss framing outperforms gain framing in B2B. 'You'll lose your installation slot in 3 weeks' > 'Book now and save time.' Frame around what they stand to lose by delaying.
psychologicalTriggers.reciprocity: Free layout plan, showroom visit, sample kit dispatch — all create psychological obligation. Make every free offering genuinely excellent.
psychologicalTriggers.socialValidation: Mention comparable clients without naming them: 'We just completed a similar project for a 60-person law firm in Sydney.' Validates the decision.
psychologicalTriggers.authority: ISO certifications, 6-year warranty, 1300 number, physical showroom — all authority signals. Lead with these before price.
psychologicalTriggers.scarcity: Installation slots genuinely fill up. Communicate this as accurate commercial intelligence, never as manufactured pressure.

trustBuildingSequence: First impression: website quality, response speed (within 4 hours), professional communication
Demonstration: showroom visit or detailed product knowledge in conversation
Social proof: reference projects, testimonials, before/after photography
Risk elimination: clear timeline, milestone payments, warranty registration
Reciprocity: free layout plan, sample kit, project walk-through
